questions.stem: What are the three phases of the agentic loop?
questions.explanation: The agentic loop is: gather context, take action, verify results. The verification phase is what separates an agent from a single model call. Without it the agent cannot tell whether its action worked, so it cannot correct course on the next iteration.

options.label: A
options.body: Gather context, take action, verify results

options.label: B
options.body: Plan, execute, report

options.label: C
options.body: Prompt, sample, decode

options.label: D
options.body: Retrieve, rank, generate

questions.stem: An agent completes a code edit and immediately reports success without running the test suite. Which phase of the agentic loop is missing?
questions.explanation: Verification is the missing phase. Taking the action (the edit) is not evidence the action achieved the goal. A verification step, such as running tests or re-reading the changed file, produces the observation the next loop iteration needs in order to self-correct.

options.label: A
options.body: Verify results

options.label: B
options.body: Gather context

options.label: C
options.body: Take action

options.label: D
options.body: Tokenize the prompt

questions.stem: You must review twelve independent files for the same class of bug. Which decomposition fits best?
questions.explanation: The twelve reviews share no data and no ordering constraint, so they are independent subtasks that can run concurrently. Wall-clock time becomes the slowest single review rather than the sum of all twelve. Sequential execution would be correct only if each review's output fed the next.

options.label: A
options.body: Parallel execution, one subtask per file

options.label: B
options.body: Strictly sequential execution, one file per turn

options.label: C
options.body: A single call containing all twelve files concatenated

options.label: D
options.body: Recursive decomposition until each subtask is a single line of code

questions.stem: In a fan-out then aggregate workflow, what does adding a barrier between stages cost you?
questions.explanation: A barrier waits for every subtask in a stage before any subtask advances, so the stage takes as long as its slowest member and fast workers sit idle. It is justified only when the next stage genuinely needs cross-item context, such as deduplicating across the whole result set.

options.label: A
options.body: Wall-clock time, because fast subtasks idle until the slowest one finishes

options.label: B
options.body: Correctness, because results arrive out of order

options.label: C
options.body: Nothing measurable; barriers are free

options.label: D
options.body: Token cost, because a barrier re-sends the full conversation

questions.stem: Which description matches a hub-and-spoke (orchestrator-worker) multi-agent topology?
questions.explanation: In hub-and-spoke a single coordinator decomposes the work, dispatches subtasks to workers, and integrates their reports. Workers do not talk to each other, which keeps the coordination logic in one place at the cost of making the hub a bottleneck.

questions.stem: Which topology is described by: each stage transforms the output of the previous stage in a fixed order?

questions.stem: What is the primary context-management benefit of delegating a research subtask to a subagent?
questions.explanation: A subagent runs in its own context window. It can read a large volume of material and return only a short report, so the orchestrator's context absorbs the conclusion rather than all the raw material. That is what makes fan-out viable on tasks too large for one window.

options.label: B

questions.stem: A subagent must act on a file the orchestrator discovered earlier in its own conversation. What must the orchestrator do?
questions.explanation: Subagents do not inherit the orchestrator's conversation history. Anything the subagent needs, such as file paths, constraints, or the expected report format, has to be stated explicitly in the delegated task. Assuming shared context is the most common cause of a subagent doing the wrong work.

options.label: B
